name: Xanadu
lede: Xanadu is a muted, greyish green named for the place word Xanadu, the legendary capital evoked by Coleridge's poem and later by the film and mansion of the same name, though the exact link to this swatch is undocumented in our sources.

sections.title: A place word, loosely attached
sections.body:
Our data classifies Xanadu as a place or institution word, but does not document which particular use of the name (Coleridge's poem, the 1980 film, or any other) the paint color is meant to evoke [1]. The name is also recorded as "Serpent" in at least one of our sources, an alternate label for the same swatch [1].

Its closest measured look-alikes are [[hydro|Hydro]] and [[serpent|Serpent]], both read as greener, and [[titmouse-blue|Titmouse Blue]], also read as greener [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 system's nearest block is greenish gray, about six units from that block's center [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds this color in 483 of them, 2.03 percent, as photographed, more common than 72 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.0 percent of that century's works, 1.9 times the expected rate, and inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, in 38 percent of its appearances [2].

Its most devoted painter is Paul Cezanne, present in 8 of the 50 Cezanne works in our archive, 6.4 times the baseline for the museums those works come from [2]. The color is also over-represented in Post-Impressionist paintings generally, at 5.0 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest match is a 1375 panel; our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2]. In printed English the word peaked in the 2000s, across all its senses, which can include non-color uses of the name [2].
